description.narrative:
The general objective of this project is to establish and strengthen a network of 10 of the 20 Community Seed Banks (CSBs) established by CTDT. The project will support local initiatives for climate adaptation, including participatory plant breeding, seed production and marketing, germplasm collection, conservation, sustainable use of local plant genetic resources, knowledge sharing on seedbanking, income savings and lending models; and local to regional to global networking. To build on previous investments from the SIDA funded Sowing Diversity = Harvesting Security program (SDHS) and likeminded projects which ran from 2014 to 2023 in Zimbabwe, CSBs have been selected from previous established farmer field schools, in the same areas of the previous project. The action intendsto establish a confederation of 10 out of the 20 community seed banks. These community seed banks will act as Knowledge and learning Hubs where farmers within and outside the area will come to learn about crop breeding techniques such as Participatory Variety Development (PVD), Participatory Variety Enhancement (PVE) and Participatory Variety Selection (PVS), community-based seed production and marketing, agroecology and other climate change mitigation and adaptation practices.The confederation of CSBs will also enhance exchange of seed and knowledge between and among farmers from the different communities e.g. during seed and food fairs. The confederation of CSBs will also facilitate the development and sharing of common management practices as contained in the Standard OperatingProcedures (SoPs) which will be developed under this project. This also provides a framework for easy coordination of community seed banking activities at national and regional level. The project will also establish information centers to improve climate change and early warning information flow from the Zimbabwe Meteorological Office and the Famine Early Warning Systems Networks (FEWSNET), especially among youths at the 10 CSBs. Weather data collected from the mini-weather stations located close to the CSBs will be provided to the FEWSNET team for their analysis and information dissemination.
Oxfam Novib will support this project through monitoring progress, finance management, providing advice and reporting to the donor.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
